chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Isḥāq ibn Jarīr, from Ḥarīz, who said:

A woman from among us asked me to admit her to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. So I sought permission for her, and he gave her permission. She entered, and with her was a female servant of hers. She said to him: O Abū ʿAbdillāh, what do you say about a woman who menstruates and then goes beyond the days of her menstruation?
He said: “If the days of her menstruation are fewer than ten days, she should wait one additional day as precaution, then she is in a state of istiḥāḍah.”

She said: But the blood continues with her for one month, two months, and three; so what should she do regarding salat? He said: “She refrains during the days of her menstruation, then performs ghusl for every two prayers.”

She said to him: The days of her menstruation vary for her, and the menstruation sometimes comes one day, two days, or three days earlier, and is delayed by a similar amount; so how is she to know it? He said: “The blood of menstruation is not unclear: it is hot blood for which she feels a burning sensation, while the blood of istiḥāḍah is corrupted, cold blood.”
He said: Then she turned to her female servant and said: Do you think he had once been a woman?

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat; the ritual prayer affected by the rulings discussed here
key_terms.الِاسْتِحَاضَةِ: istiḥāḍah; irregular non-menstrual bleeding with separate legal rulings
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation; the legally recognized menstrual bleeding with its rulings
key_terms.بَارِدٌ: cold; describing the blood of istiḥāḍah in this narration
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلُ: she performs ghusl; the ritual bath required in the described circumstance
key_terms.حُرْقَةً: a burning sensation felt with menstrual blood
key_terms.دَمُ الْحَيْضِ: menstrual blood, identified here by its distinguishing qualities
key_terms.مُسْتَحَاضَةٌ: a woman in the state of istiḥāḍah, experiencing non-menstrual irregular bleeding

ai.seo_question: How does a woman distinguish between ḥayḍ and istiḥāḍah, and what are the prayer rulings when bleeding continues?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal discussion with Imām Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the rulings of ḥayḍ and istiḥāḍah, especially when bleeding extends beyond normal menstrual days or becomes irregular. It explains how a woman distinguishes menstrual blood from istiḥāḍah and outlines the related rulings for salat and ghusl.
